newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Repco charged with securities violation.
newsitem.headline: Repco charged with securities violation.

text.p: Timber and gaming concern Repco Holdings Bhd was charged in a local court on Friday with making a misleading statement that could influence trading in its stock, Malaysian newspapers reported on Saturday.
They said the company, which was represented by its senior manager, Huang Tek Hooi, pleaded not guilty.
The company, which is listed on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's (KLSE) Second Board, is charged with committing the offence on January 27, 1996.
Officials at Repco could not be reached for comment. Its stock was off 50 cents to 81.50 in Friday afternoon trading.

Last month, Repco's chief executive officer was charged in the same offence. Choo Chin Thye pleaded not guilty to the charge, which carries a maximum fine of one million ringgit or 10 years' jail on conviction.
Choo's signature appears on a letter dated January 27, 1996 sent from Repco to the KLSE outlining a profit forecast for the years ending June 30, 1996 and June 30, 1997.

But a week after issuing that forecast, the company withdrew the letter and issued a lower profit projection, saying it had prematurely assumed approvals for a new gaming license which were still pending.

Judge Zura Yahya allowed the Securities Commission's application for a joint trial after being informed that both offences were committed at the same place and time and the witnesses and documents involved were the same, Bernama said.
The court then set December 27 to fix the trial date, Bernama said.
Zura also allowed Choo bail of 50,000 ringgit in two sureties and ordered that his travel documents be surrendered to the court as a condition for bail.
